slowest_experiments.label: Exp 219: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Sequential model loading — Qwen then Gemma loaded onto GPU 0 serially; GPU 1 idle throughout. Each model required full VRAM allocation before the previous was freed. No DualGPURunner in place at this stage of the milestone sequence.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 308: JEPA fast-path gate integration (tests failing checkpoint)
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Interrupted conductor run left the test suite in a failing state. Recovery required full context reload, triage of new vs pre-existing failures, re-run of 3000+ test suite, and re-commit — adding ~30-40 min diagnostic overhead on top of the experiment itself. No partial-result fast-path existed.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 184: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: 3B-parameter model requires 4x the VRAM and per-token latency vs the 0.8B baseline. Verify-repair loop runs 3 forward passes per question on a single GPU (verify + repair + re-verify). No inference batching to amortize model loading. GPU 1 idle throughout.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 221: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Sequential pipeline across prompt variants with no batching. Typed IR prompts are significantly longer than GSM8K prompts, raising per-call token cost and reducing effective throughput. Constraint evaluation was single-threaded.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 425: Conductor timeout watchdog — RETRO-003 (17+ milestone carry)
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Implementing the timeout watchdog, deferred for 17+ milestones, required writing ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog from scratch with 35 tests, spec updates, and template integration. Reading 17-milestone RETRO-003 history added substantial overhead. The delay multiplied the implementation cost.

bottlenecks_identified: GPU 0 zombie memory saturation (97% VRAM, 23774MB, 0% utilization at milestone end): three stale processes (PIDs 145715/254433/289150) held 23.7GB on GPU 0 continuously. The longest-running zombie had wall_time=41335s (~11.5 hours) while contributing near-zero compute. Subsequent experiments likely suffered VRAM pressure, triggering fallbacks or OOM-driven slowdowns throughout the milestone.

GPU 1 completely idle for the entire milestone: GPU 1 showed 6MB VRAM at 0% utilization at milestone end — effectively unused. With dual RTX 3090s available (48GB total VRAM), all inference ran on a single GPU, halving hardware effective throughput. No DualGPURunner was wired into the conductor.

Repeated re-verification of already-implemented code: at least 4 experiments (Exps 439, 444, 446, 447) were re-verified in separate sessions with no code changes between runs. Exp 447 (KAEMEnergy) was verified three times across three separate sessions. Each re-verification consumed 8-20 minutes of file reads and test re-runs with no new output produced.

RETRO-003 (timeout watchdog) carried 17+ milestones before Exp 425: runaway experiments were not killed automatically throughout the earlier phases of this milestone. Estimated 3-5 runaway experiments x 45 min average overshoot = 135-225 minutes of wasted GPU time and thermal stress before ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog shipped.

Three missing result deliverables (Exps 450, 451, 455): experiments completed but result JSON files were absent at milestone end (RETRO-032, RETRO-033, RETRO-036). The headline milestone question — 'did we get the first positive verify-repair number?' — could not be confirmed due to the missing Exp 451 artifact. Root cause: deliverable-path mismatch between conductor task spec and experiment script output path.

Scaffolding-only experiments inflating the completed count: a significant fraction of the 296 experiments reached status=scaffolding_only or LIVE RUN PENDING, meaning harnesses were built but no live GPU result was obtained. Experiment count inflates without advancing measured research outcomes.

Pre-flight test suite overhead on doc-only changes: the full 3900+ test suite triggered after every commit, including changelog and ops doc updates. At 60-90s per run and approximately 80 doc-only commits in a 296-experiment milestone, this adds 80-120 minutes of unnecessary test overhead per milestone.

Conductor checkpoint interruptions with no structured recovery: when sessions were interrupted, no partial-result state was serialized. The next session re-reads full context, identifies what was and was not committed, and re-runs the test suite — adding 30-40 min per incident (cf. Exp 308 at 105 min).

Zero adoption of improvements identified in prior retro: the .33 retro identified 10 specific improvements estimated at 32% total time savings. None were implemented in time to affect milestone .34. Actual wall-time reduction was 2.3% (5002 to 4886 min). Retro work is not self-applying — it requires explicit conductor task budget.

Sequential conductor with no inter-experiment parallelism: experiments ran strictly serially. Multi-GPU hardware sat idle between experiment teardown and next startup. Inter-experiment gap (cleanup + commit + context load) estimated at 2-4 min x 296 experiments = 10-20 hours of potential parallel opportunity.
improvements_suggested: Kill zombie GPU processes at conductor session start: add a startup hook that calls gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies (already implemented) before the first experiment of every session. This recovers VRAM immediately and prevents GPU 0 saturation from degrading subsequent experiments. Estimated savings: 0-30 min recovery time per session, plus reduced OOM-driven fallback overhead throughout the milestone.

Add ExperimentTemplate.assert_deliverable_written() called as the final statement of every experiment main(): if self._output_path does not exist after build_result() returns, raise FileNotFoundError loudly before the process exits. This directly prevents RETRO-032, RETRO-033, and RETRO-036 from occurring in milestone .35. Zero-tolerance policy for silent deliverable drops.

Wire DualGPURunner into experiment_template.py for all dual-model experiments: assign model A to cuda:0 and model B to cuda:1 with explicit device_map={'': 'cuda:N'}. Run both models in parallel threads during inference phases. Estimated throughput improvement on dual-model benchmarks: 1.5-1.8x. This addresses the entire Exp 219 (117 min) class of bottleneck.

Add conductor deduplication check before scheduling each experiment: before starting experiment N, check if results/experiment_N*.json exists and honest_verdict is not 'partial' or 'blocked'. If healthy results exist, skip re-implementation. Prevents the Exp 447 triple-re-verification pattern. Estimated savings: 8-20 min x 4 re-verified experiments = 32-80 min per milestone.

Implement doc-only commit classifier to skip the full test suite: if the diff touches only *.md, docs/, ops/, _bmad/, skip the 3900+ test suite and run only ruff + mypy (5-10s total). Estimated savings: 80-120 min of unnecessary test overhead per milestone.

Add conductor session health check as the first action of every session: verify CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE propagates to subprocesses, both GPUs are under 200MB VRAM and idle, and no zombie processes exist. If any check fails, auto-remediate (kill zombies, re-export env) before proceeding. Estimated savings: 60-90 min per milestone where env propagation is broken (cf. RETRO-022, 6-milestone block).

Implement per-experiment partial-result handoff on interruption: when the conductor is interrupted (SIGTERM, exception, timeout), automatically serialize partial ExperimentTemplate state to results/experiment_NNN_partial.json before exit. The next session fast-paths to resume rather than triaging from scratch. Estimated recovery time reduction: 30-40 min per interrupted experiment.

Enforce inference batching in all benchmark harnesses: batch_size=8 for GSM8K (50 questions), batch_size=4 for HumanEval (longer prompts). BatchedInferenceRunner already exists in experiment_template.py — use it consistently. Expected 3-5x reduction in per-question inference latency at current GPU utilization levels.

Allocate explicit conductor task budget for retro improvements each milestone: track which improvements from the prior retro were implemented. A 0/10 adoption rate (as in .33 to .34) means retro work is pure documentation. Reserve 2-3 experiment slots per milestone exclusively for implementing prior-retro items. Report adoption rate in every operational retro.

Add GPU thermal throttle gate: if any GPU exceeds 80C, pause conductor and open a RETRO item. Do not start the next experiment until temperature drops to 70C. RTX 3090 observed at 82C during runaway experiments — sustained operation near thermal limits shortens hardware lifetime and may corrupt results.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: Top contributors (all from unimplemented .33 retro items still applicable): DualGPURunner parallelism on dual-model experiments (~8%), inference batching (~6%), conductor health check preventing env-propagation blocks (~5%), doc-only test-skip classifier (~4%), zombie kill at session start (~4%), partial-result fast-path on interruptions (~4%), deduplication preventing re-verification cycles (~4%). New item from .34 analysis: assert_deliverable_written() preventing missing-artifact milestones (~2% — prevents the headline question from being unanswerable for a third consecutive milestone). Combined estimated reduction: approximately 35% of total wall time, bringing a comparable 296-experiment milestone from 4886 min to approximately 3176 min (~53 hours vs current ~81 hours).

meta_reflection: Milestone 2026.04.34 ran only 2.3% faster than .33 despite identifying 32% savings potential in the prior retro. Zero of those improvements were implemented. The same structural bottlenecks — zombie GPU processes, sequential model loading, missing deliverables, re-verification cycles — are compounding across milestones. The critical new signal is that three experiment result files were missing at milestone end, leaving the headline research question ('first positive verify-repair number?') unanswerable for the third consecutive milestone. Process debt has reached the point where it directly blocks research outcomes, not merely slows them. The two highest-leverage actions for milestone .35 are: (1) implement assert_deliverable_written() to enforce zero-tolerance for missing result files, and (2) allocate explicit conductor task budget for retro improvements so that the 35% efficiency gain estimated here is actually captured.
